# Disposable Diaper Structure with Enhanced Stretchable Side Regions

## Overview of the Outer Member Configuration

The disposable diaper disclosed herein incorporates outer members specifically engineered with stretchable regions strategically positioned adjacent to the inner edges of the side seal portions, extending in the width direction of the garment. This configuration ensures that the areas most critical for fit and comfort—namely, the regions surrounding the side seals—benefit from enhanced elasticity and conformability to the wearer's body contours.

## Structural Composition of the Stretchable Regions

Each stretchable region is constructed from two distinct sheet layers between which a plurality of elongated elastically stretchable members are disposed. These elastic members are arranged in a systematic manner, spaced at predetermined intervals along the front-back direction of the diaper, while each individual member extends across the width direction. This arrangement allows the stretchable regions to provide consistent, distributed elasticity across the relevant portions of the garment rather than concentrated points of stretch, thereby promoting a more uniform and comfortable fit.

## Attachment Mechanism of the Elastic Members

A defining characteristic of each elastically stretchable member is its dual-point fixation design. Specifically, each elastic member possesses two fixed ends, both of which are securely attached to the surrounding sheet layers. In contrast, the central or middle portion of each elastic member remains deliberately unfixed and free from attachment to either sheet layer. This selective fixation pattern—securing only the terminal ends while leaving the middle section unbonded—is essential to preserving the stretchability and elastic recovery properties of the member, as the unfixed middle section can freely elongate and contract in response to movement and body dynamics without being constrained by adhesive or bonding forces.

## Bonding Configuration Between Sheet Layers

Beyond the fixation points of the elastic members themselves, the two sheet layers comprising the stretchable region are also joined to one another through additional welding operations. These sheet-to-sheet bonding sections are deliberately positioned in the spaces located between adjacent elastically stretchable members, oriented along the front-back direction of the diaper. This intermediate bonding serves to maintain the structural integrity and layered cohesion of the stretchable region while preserving the functional independence of each elastic member's unfixed middle section.

## Design Constraint Regarding Bonding Section Placement

A particularly noteworthy structural feature of this design is the deliberate exclusion of any sheet bonding section that protrudes into or extends from the side seal portion within the stretchable regions. This design constraint ensures that the welding points joining the two sheet layers remain confined within the boundaries of the stretchable region itself, without encroaching upon or interfering with the side seal portion. By preventing such protrusion, the design avoids the creation of rigid or non-stretchable zones near the side seals that could otherwise compromise the elasticity, comfort, and overall functional performance of the stretchable region adjacent to this critical structural boundary.

# Underpants-Type Disposable Diaper with Enhanced Stretchable Side Regions

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to an underpants-type disposable diaper, and more particularly to an improved structural configuration for the outer member of such diapers that enhances fit, comfort, and wearability while maintaining robust structural integrity at critical seam locations.

## Background

Underpants-type disposable diapers typically comprise a front body panel and a back body panel that are joined together at side seal portions to form leg openings and a waist opening, creating a garment-like structure similar to conventional underwear. The outer member of such diapers, which contacts the wearer's skin or forms the outermost visible layer, often incorporates elastic members to provide a snug, comfortable fit around the wearer's waist and torso.

Conventional designs have faced challenges in balancing the need for effective elasticity with the requirement for durable, reliable seam construction at the side seal portions. In many prior configurations, bonding sections used to join the sheet layers together can inadvertently protrude into or interfere with the side seal portions, creating discomfort, potential irritation points, or weakened structural integrity precisely where the diaper experiences the most mechanical stress during wear and movement.

## Detailed Description of the Configuration

### Structural Overview

The underpants-type disposable diaper described herein features an outer member constructed with specifically engineered stretchable regions positioned adjacent to the side seal portions. This outer member is fundamentally composed of two sheet layers between which multiple elastic members are sandwiched, extending in the width direction of the diaper (i.e., transverse to the longitudinal body axis, running circumferentially around the wearer's torso).

### Elastic Member Configuration

Each elastic member within the stretchable region is fixed to the surrounding sheet layers only at its two endpoints. Critically, along the entire middle section of each elastic member—the portion between these two fixed endpoints—the elastic member remains unattached and unbonded to either of the two sheet layers. This creates a design wherein the elastic member can contract and expand somewhat independently along its length, generating localized elasticity and gathering effects when the elastic member is in its relaxed, contracted state.

This partial-attachment approach differs from configurations in which elastic members are bonded continuously or at multiple points along their length, which tends to create more rigid, less naturally conforming stretch characteristics. By anchoring only the endpoints, the elastic members can generate a more supple, cloth-like gathering pattern that better conforms to the wearer's body contours.

### Sheet Bonding Sections

Between adjacent elastic members—that is, in the spaces separating one width-direction elastic member from the next—the two sheet layers are welded together at discrete bonding sections. These bonding sections serve to maintain the structural cohesion of the two-layer sheet assembly, preventing the layers from separating or shifting relative to one another in the areas where no elastic member is present to help maintain the sandwich structure.

The welding process used to create these bonding sections may employ heat sealing, ultrasonic welding, or other suitable joining techniques known in the art of nonwoven and film material bonding, provided that the resulting bond is sufficiently durable for the intended use while not introducing excessive rigidity or discomfort in the gathered stretchable regions.

### Positional Relationship to Side Seal Portions

A key feature of this configuration is the precise spatial relationship between the sheet bonding sections and the side seal portions. Specifically, within the stretchable regions of the outer member, none of the sheet bonding sections are positioned such that they protrude outward from or extend into the side seal portion itself.

This is achieved through careful design of the placement pattern of the elastic members and their corresponding endpoint attachment points, as well as the spacing and location of the inter-elastic bonding sections. By ensuring that all bonding sections remain confined within the stretchable region proper—rather than extending into or crossing the boundary of the side seal portion—the design avoids creating stiff, non-stretchable intrusions into what would otherwise be a uniformly flexible seam area.

## Advantages and Technical Effects

### Improved Fit and Comfort

The described configuration enables the stretchable regions to provide effective, localized elasticity precisely where needed—around the waist or leg openings—without being compromised by rigid bonding points that might otherwise interrupt the smooth gathering and stretching action. Because each elastic member is free to move along its unattached middle section, the resulting fabric behavior more closely mimics natural, soft fabric gathering rather than the stiffer behavior associated with fully bonded elastic strands.

### Maintained Structural Integrity at Seams

Simultaneously, because no sheet bonding sections protrude into the side seal portions, the side seals themselves remain uncompromised by the presence of these welding points. This is significant because side seal portions are typically formed through their own separate bonding or welding process (often involving heat sealing or ultrasonic welding of the front and back panels together), and the introduction of additional, potentially misaligned or protruding bonding sections from the stretchable region could otherwise weaken the seal, create uneven thickness, or introduce discomfort at the seam edge, which is often in direct contact with the wearer's skin at the hip or side of the body.

### Balanced Design Philosophy

Overall, this configuration reflects a design philosophy that seeks to isolate and separately optimize two distinct functional zones within the outer member: the stretchable region, optimized for elasticity and gentle gathering through the endpoint-only attachment of elastic members, and the side seal portion, optimized for secure, reliable, and comfortable bonding between the front and back panels of the diaper. By preventing overlap or interference between the bonding sections associated with these two zones, the diaper achieves both improved elastic performance and reliable seam strength without one function compromising the other.

This structural approach represents a refinement over conventional designs, offering wearers a disposable diaper that combines the practical benefits of secure construction with the comfort characteristics increasingly expected from modern absorbent garment products.

# The Word "The"

"The" is the most commonly used word in the English language, yet it rarely draws attention to itself. As a definite article, its job is simple but essential: it points to something specific, something already known or about to be identified. When we say "the book" rather than "a book," we signal that we mean a particular book—not just any book, but *the* one under discussion.

Despite its brevity, "the" carries surprising weight in shaping meaning. Consider the difference between "I saw a dog" and "I saw the dog." The first introduces a dog into the conversation for the first time; the second assumes the listener already knows which dog is meant. This small distinction reflects how language tracks shared knowledge between speaker and listener.

Linguistically, "the" is classified as a function word rather than a content word. Unlike nouns, verbs, or adjectives, it doesn't carry rich, standalone meaning. Instead, it works quietly in the background, organizing and clarifying the relationships between other words. Function words like "the" are often overlooked in casual speech, yet they are indispensable to fluent, natural-sounding English.

Interestingly, not all languages have an equivalent to "the." Russian, Japanese, and many other languages manage perfectly well without a direct translation, relying instead on context, word order, or other grammatical cues to convey definiteness. This makes "the" a distinctly English challenge for language learners, who often struggle to grasp when to use it, when to use "a" or "an," and when to omit an article altogether.

Ultimately, "the" exemplifies how the smallest words can perform outsized roles in communication. It requires no dictionary definition of its own beyond grammatical function, yet without it, English would sound stilted, ambiguous, or foreign. Its constant, unassuming presence in nearly every sentence we write or speak reminds us that meaning often depends not just on the big, dramatic words, but on the tiny threads that hold our sentences together.

# PATENT SPECIFICATION

## Detailed Description of the Preferred Embodiment

**[0001]** Referring now to the accompanying drawings, an underpants-type disposable diaper 1 according to the present embodiment will be described in detail. The diaper 1 comprises a front waist region 10, a rear waist region 20, and a crotch region 30 interposed between the front waist region 10 and the rear waist region 20, the crotch region 30 including a liquid-absorbent main body 40 extending longitudinally therethrough.

**[0002]** The front waist region 10 includes a first outer member 11 and the rear waist region 20 includes a second outer member 21, each of the first outer member 11 and the second outer member 21 comprising an outer sheet layer 12, 22 disposed on a garment-facing exterior side and an inner sheet layer 13, 23 disposed on a skin-facing interior side, the outer sheet layer 12, 22 and the inner sheet layer 13, 23 being joined together at a plurality of intermittent bonding sections 14, 24 so as to define therebetween a housing space accommodating a plurality of elastic members 15, 25 in a stretched state.

**[0003]** The elastic members 15, 25 are disposed in a substantially waist-encircling direction, i.e., a lateral direction substantially orthogonal to the longitudinal direction of the diaper 1, and are fixed to at least one of the outer sheet layer 12, 22 and the inner sheet layer 13, 23 at the bonding sections 14, 24, whereby the front waist region 10 and the rear waist region 20 constitute stretchable side panels 16, 26 capable of expanding and contracting in the lateral direction to conform to the wearer's body.

**[0004]** The first outer member 11 forming the front waist region 10 and the second outer member 21 forming the rear waist region 20 are joined to each other at a pair of side seal sections 17, the side seal sections 17 being formed by overlapping side edge portions 18, 28 of the first outer member 11 and the second outer member 21, respectively, and bonding the overlapping side edge portions 18, 28 by heat sealing, ultrasonic sealing, or an adhesive, thereby forming a waist opening 2 and a pair of leg openings 3, 3 in the assembled underpants-type disposable diaper 1.

**[0005]** In a preferred embodiment, the bonding sections 14, 24 are arranged in a plurality of rows extending in the longitudinal direction and spaced apart from one another in the lateral direction, each row of bonding sections 14, 24 being disposed between adjacent elastic members 15, 25 so as to prevent the elastic members 15, 25 from shifting or bunching within the housing space during stretching and contraction, thereby imparting a uniform gathering effect to the stretchable side panels 16, 26 and enhancing the fit of the diaper 1 about the waist and hip regions of the wearer.

**[0006]** It should be noted that the outer sheet layer 12, 22 and the inner sheet layer 13, 23 may each be formed of a nonwoven fabric, and that the elastic members 15, 25 may be constituted by a plurality of elastic strands, an elastic film, or an elastic nonwoven fabric, without departing from the scope of the present invention as defined by the appended claims.

# Technical Description: Elastic Member Fixation in Side Seal Stretchable Regions

## Structural Configuration

In the side seal regions of the diaper, the elastic members **19** are disposed in a stretched state between the front-side sheet layer **12F** and the back-side sheet layer **12B**, both of which extend outwardly from the main body of the absorbent article to form the side seal flaps. These sheet layers **12F** and **12B** are preferably formed of a nonwoven fabric, a laminate of nonwoven fabric and film, or a similar flexible sheet material having sufficient tensile strength to withstand repeated stretching during wear.

## Elastic Member Arrangement

The elastic members **19** comprise a plurality of elongate strands, such as elastomeric threads or ribbons, arranged substantially parallel to one another and extending in the width direction (or, in certain embodiments, the longitudinal direction) of the side seal region. Each elastic member **19** is maintained in an elastically stretched state, having an elongation ratio in the range of approximately 150% to 350% relative to its natural, relaxed length, prior to being fixed between the sheet layers **12F** and **12B**.

## Bonding/Fixation Structure

The fixation between the front-side sheet **12F**, the elastic members **19**, and the back-side sheet **12B** is achieved through a bonding region **20**, which may be formed by:

1. **Adhesive bonding** — a hot-melt adhesive applied in a pattern (e.g., spiral, slot-coat, or bead pattern) between the sheet layers **12F**, **12B** and the elastic members **19**, such that the adhesive penetrates and anchors the elastic strands while simultaneously laminating the two sheets together;

2. **Thermal/ultrasonic welding** — a plurality of discrete or continuous weld points/lines **20** formed by applying heat and pressure, or ultrasonic energy, through the sheet layers **12F** and **12B**, thereby fusing the sheets to one another and mechanically entrapping the elastic members **19** at intervals along their length.

The bonding region **20** is preferably configured as a plurality of discrete fixation points or lines spaced along the longitudinal direction of each elastic member **19**, rather than a single continuous bond line, so as to permit localized flexibility and reduce stress concentration at the fixation sites while maintaining reliable anchoring of the elastic members **19** during repeated extension and contraction.

## Functional Effect

By virtue of this bonding structure **20**, when the elastic members **19** contract from their stretched state after fixation, the surrounding non-bonded portions of the sheet layers **12F** and **12B** are drawn together and gathered, forming a plurality of fine gathers or pleats in the side seal region. This gathering imparts elasticity and conformability to the side seal stretchable region, enabling the side panels to expand and contract in accordance with the wearer's body movements, thereby improving fit around the waist and leg openings while preventing leakage and enhancing wearing comfort.

## Manufacturing Consideration

In a preferred embodiment, the elastic members **19** are fed and stretched to the prescribed elongation ratio prior to being interposed between the continuously advancing webs of sheet layers **12F** and **12B**; the bonding region **20** is thereafter formed by passing the laminate through a pair of embossing rolls, ultrasonic horn/anvil assembly, or adhesive application station, such that the elastic members **19** are fixed in their stretched condition at predetermined intervals corresponding to the desired gather pitch in the finished side seal stretchable region.

---

*Note: Reference numerals used herein (12F, 12B, 19, 20) are illustrative and should correspond to consistent labeling throughout the accompanying drawings and full specification.*

# Claim Language: Elastically Stretchable Members and Sheet Bonding Sections in Diaper Side Panels

## Sample Independent Claim

**Claim 1.** A disposable diaper comprising:

a chassis having a front waist region, a back waist region, and a crotch region disposed therebetween;

a pair of side panels disposed on at least one of the front waist region and the back waist region, each of the side panels extending in a width direction toward a side edge of the diaper and terminating at a side seal configured to join the front waist region and the back waist region;

each of the side panels comprising a first sheet and a second sheet joined to each other so as to define a stretchable region therebetween;

a plurality of elastically stretchable members disposed between the first sheet and the second sheet in the stretchable region, the elastically stretchable members extending in the width direction and being arranged at intervals in a longitudinal direction orthogonal to the width direction;

a plurality of sheet bonding sections formed between the first sheet and the second sheet, the sheet bonding sections being disposed so as to bond the first sheet and the second sheet together independently of the elastically stretchable members;

wherein each of the sheet bonding sections is disposed at a position spaced inward, in the width direction, from the side seal such that no portion of any sheet bonding section extends beyond the side seal in the width direction.

---

## Sample Dependent Claims

**Claim 2.** The disposable diaper according to claim 1, wherein the sheet bonding sections are arranged intermittently along the longitudinal direction between adjacent ones of the elastically stretchable members.

**Claim 3.** The disposable diaper according to claim 1, wherein each of the sheet bonding sections is positioned at an innermost side-directional location relative to the side seal that is closer, in the width direction, to a center of the diaper than an outermost width-direction edge of the side seal.

**Claim 4.** The disposable diaper according to claim 1, wherein the elastically stretchable members extend continuously to a position overlapping the side seal in the width direction, while the sheet bonding sections terminate at a position that does not overlap the side seal.

**Claim 5.** The disposable diaper according to claim 1, wherein the plurality of sheet bonding sections are arranged in a staggered pattern in the longitudinal direction so as not to align with the elastically stretchable members at a same longitudinal position.

**Claim 6.** The disposable diaper according to claim 1, wherein the side seal comprises a heat-sealed region formed by welding the first sheet and the second sheet of the front waist region to a corresponding first sheet and second sheet of the back waist region, and wherein the sheet bonding sections are formed at a manufacturing step separate from formation of the side seal.

**Claim 7.** The disposable diaper according to claim 1, wherein a width-direction distance between an outermost one of the sheet bonding sections and the side seal is greater than zero and less than a width-direction distance between adjacent elastically stretchable members.

---

## Notes on Claim Drafting Rationale

- **Claim 1** establishes the core structural relationship: bonding sections are affirmatively limited to a region *inward* of the side seal, explicitly excluding any extension beyond it. This "no portion extends beyond" language creates a clear infringement boundary and distinguishes over prior art where bonding may reach or cross the seal.

- **Dependent claims 2–3** narrow the spatial arrangement (intermittent, innermost positioning) to support varying embodiments disclosed in the specification.

- **Claim 4** creates a contrast between the elastic members (which may extend to/through the seal region) and the bonding sections (which may not), emphasizing the functional distinction between the two features — useful for supporting an argument that this arrangement prevents interference with seal integrity or reduces stiffness at the seam.

- **Claim 5** covers a staggered/offset embodiment, useful if the specification shows the bonding sections avoiding direct overlap with the elastic strands.

- **Claim 6** ties the bonding sections to a distinct manufacturing step (e.g., ultrasonic or heat-embossing) separate from the side-seal welding process, which can support a **process limitation** argument.

- **Claim 7** provides a quantitative/relative distance limitation as a fallback position, useful for claim differentiation during prosecution.

---

Would you like me to also draft:
1. A **method claim** for manufacturing this arrangement, or
2. **Figures-style claim language** referencing reference numerals (e.g., "10," "20a–20n") as typically seen in Japanese-style diaper patents (Kao, Unicharm, P&G format), or
3. Alternative claim language emphasizing a **specific technical effect** (e.g., preventing seal peeling, improving fit, reducing skin irritation) to anchor claims to a utility argument?

# Disposable Pant-Type Diaper: Outer Member Construction with Elastic Strand Placement

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to a disposable pant-type wearing article, and more particularly to the construction of an outer cover member incorporating elongate elastic members disposed between sheet layers, wherein such elastic members include both fixed segments bonded to the surrounding sheets and unfixed segments free from such bonding, thereby imparting selective, zone-differentiated contractile force to the article.

---

## Background

Pant-type disposable diapers conventionally comprise a chassis including a liquid-permeable topsheet, a liquid-impermeable backsheet, an absorbent body interposed therebetween, and a pair of side panel members or an outer cover member joined at side edges to form a waist opening and a pair of leg openings. To provide fit and gasketing function around the wearer's waist and legs, elastic strands are incorporated into the outer member. However, uniform elastic contraction across the entire outer member can cause excessive gathering, discomfort, and diminished absorbent body contact in regions where stretch is unnecessary or undesirable, such as the front and rear waist center regions abutting the absorbent body, or regions requiring print pattern stability. There exists a need for a construction that permits localized control of elastic contraction through selective fixation of elastic strands within a laminated outer member.

---

## Summary

According to one embodiment, a pant-type disposable diaper is provided comprising:

1. A chassis extending in a longitudinal direction and a transverse direction orthogonal thereto, having a front waist region, a rear waist region, and a crotch region interposed between the front and rear waist regions;
2. An absorbent main body disposed in the crotch region and extending partially into the front and rear waist regions;
3. An outer member disposed at least in the front waist region and the rear waist region, the outer member comprising a first sheet layer and a second sheet layer joined together with a plurality of elastic strands disposed therebetween in the transverse direction; and
4. The plurality of elastic strands each comprising, along their longitudinal extent, at least one fixed section bonded to at least one of the first sheet layer and the second sheet layer, and at least one unfixed section not bonded to either sheet layer, the unfixed section being disposed so as to overlap the absorbent main body in the transverse direction.

By this construction, the outer member contracts in the transverse direction at the fixed sections to form gathers that conform to the wearer's torso, while the unfixed sections, positioned in overlapping relation to the absorbent main body, remain substantially non-contractive, thereby suppressing puckering of the absorbent body and preserving planar contact against the wearer's skin.

---

## Detailed Description

### 1. Overall Configuration

Referring to the drawings, the pant-type disposable diaper 1 includes a front waist region S1, a rear waist region S2, and a crotch region S3 located between the front and rear waist regions in the longitudinal direction L. The diaper further defines a transverse direction W orthogonal to the longitudinal direction. The chassis includes an absorbent main body 10 comprising a liquid-permeable topsheet 11, a liquid-impermeable or liquid-resistant backsheet 12, and an absorbent core 13 disposed between the topsheet and the backsheet.

The outer member 20 is disposed outward (relative to the wearer) of the backsheet 12 in at least the front waist region S1 and the rear waist region S2, and in some embodiments extends continuously through the crotch region S3 as well. The outer member 20 comprises a first sheet layer 21 (which may constitute a skin-facing side sheet) and a second sheet layer 22 (which may constitute a garment-facing side sheet), the first and second sheet layers being joined to one another at a plurality of bonding regions, such as by adhesive application, heat sealing, or ultrasonic bonding, so as to define a laminate structure with an interior space therebetween.

### 2. Elastic Strand Arrangement

A plurality of elastic strands 30 (also referred to as elastic members or waist elastics) are disposed within the interior space between the first sheet layer 21 and the second sheet layer 22, each elastic strand 30 extending substantially in the transverse direction W and being arranged in a spaced-apart relationship along the longitudinal direction L so as to define a plurality of parallel elastic strands, for example, from 3 to 30 strands, though the number is not particularly limited.

Each elastic strand 30 is provided in a stretched state at the time of assembly and is disposed between the first sheet layer 21 and second sheet layer 22 such that, upon relaxation, the elastic strand 30 induces contraction of the surrounding sheet material at locations where the strand is bonded thereto.

#### 2.1 Fixed Sections

Each elastic strand 30 includes at least one fixed section 31 at which the elastic strand 30 is bonded to at least one, and preferably both, of the first sheet layer 21 and second sheet layer 22 by way of an adhesive, such as a hot-melt adhesive applied in a bead, spiral, or slot-coated pattern. The fixed sections 31 are preferably disposed at transversely outboard locations corresponding to the side regions of the front waist region S1 and rear waist region S2, i.e., the regions disposed laterally outward of the absorbent main body 10, and further correspond to the side seal regions 40 at which the front waist region S1 and rear waist region S2 are joined to one another to form the pant-type side seams.

At the fixed sections 31, the elastic strand 30 remains in tension and, being bonded to the sheet layers, causes the first sheet layer 21 and second sheet layer 22 to contract and gather in the transverse direction W upon relaxation of the elastic strand following assembly, thereby producing a waist gasketing effect that conforms elastically about the wearer's torso circumference.

#### 2.2 Unfixed Sections

Each elastic strand 30 further includes at least one unfixed section 32, disposed longitudinally between fixed sections 31 (or between a fixed section 31 and a strand terminus), at which the elastic strand 30 is not bonded to either the first sheet layer 21 or the second sheet layer 22. The unfixed section 32 is positioned so as to overlap, in the transverse direction W, the absorbent main body 10 — that is, the unfixed section 32 is located inboard of the fixed sections 31 and spans the transverse width corresponding to the placement of the absorbent core 13 and its associated topsheet/backsheet assembly.

Because the unfixed section 32 is not adhered to the surrounding sheet layers, the contractile force of the elastic strand 30 at this location is not transmitted to the first sheet layer 21 or second sheet layer 22. Consequently, the sheet layers in the region overlapping the absorbent main body 10 remain substantially flat and non-gathered, notwithstanding the continued elastic tension present within the strand itself along its unfixed length.

In certain embodiments, the elastic strand 30 may be severed at, or immediately adjacent to, the boundary of the unfixed section 32, such that no residual tension is transmitted across the absorbent main body overlap region; alternatively, the elastic strand 30 may remain continuous and merely unbonded through the unfixed section 32, permitting the strand to freely retract within the interior space between the sheet layers without engaging said sheet layers.

### 3. Transitional Configuration

In a further embodiment, each elastic strand 30 may include a transition section disposed between a fixed section 31 and an adjacent unfixed section 32, at which the degree of bonding is intermediate — for example, an intermittent bonding pattern providing partial adhesion — such that the contraction gradient between the gathered side regions and the flat central region is gradual rather than abrupt, thereby reducing localized stress concentration and improving wearer comfort at the transition boundary.

### 4. Additional Configurational Variations

# Elastic Waistband/Side Panel Structure for Disposable Diapers
## Technical Description of Width-Direction Elastic Members and Bonding Configuration

### 1. Field of the Invention

This description relates to an absorbent article, specifically a disposable diaper or pant-type diaper, having a plurality of width-direction (transverse) elastic members disposed in the front and/or rear waist regions, configured to provide circumferential stretch while maintaining structural integrity at the side seal regions.

---

### 2. Background Structural Configuration

The diaper body comprises:

- A **front waist panel** and a **rear waist panel**, each including an outer nonwoven layer and an inner nonwoven layer (or a backsheet and topsheet composite) defining a laminate structure;
- A plurality of **width-direction elastic members** (e.g., elastomeric strands, ribbons, or films) interposed between the outer and inner nonwoven layers, extending substantially in the width direction (i.e., the direction connecting the left and right side edges of the diaper, substantially orthogonal to the longitudinal, front-to-back direction);
- **Side seal regions** located at or near the left and right side edges of the front and rear waist panels, where the front panel is joined to the rear panel to form the pant-like structure (in the case of pant-type diapers), or where side flaps are joined via fastening tapes (in the case of tape-type diapers).

---

### 3. Configuration of the Width-Direction Elastic Members

#### 3.1 General Arrangement

The width-direction elastic members are arranged in parallel, spaced apart from one another in the longitudinal (vertical/height) direction of the waist panel, each elastic member extending continuously across substantially the entire width of the panel, from the first side edge to the second side edge.

Each elastic member is affixed to at least one of the outer or inner nonwoven layers by an adhesive (e.g., a hot-melt elastic attachment adhesive) applied in a spiral, slit-coat, or bead pattern, such that the elastic member remains bonded to the nonwoven substrate along substantially its entire length, excluding designated non-bonded (free) regions if present for gathering purposes.

#### 3.2 Fixed Ends of the Elastic Members

Each width-direction elastic member has a **first fixed end** and a **second fixed end**, located respectively at or adjacent to the first side edge and the second side edge of the waist panel.

- The **fixed ends** are defined as the terminal portions of the elastic member at which the elastic member is secured against retraction, either by:
  (a) direct thermal or ultrasonic fusion of the elastic member to the nonwoven layers at the side seal region, or
  (b) adhesive fixation reinforced by a compressed/heat-sealed nonwoven laminate at the side edge, forming a **non-stretchable end zone**.

- The fixed ends are positioned such that they coincide with, or are contained within, the **side seal region**, so that upon formation of the side seal (via ultrasonic welding, heat sealing, or high-frequency welding), the elastic member's terminal portion is captured and immobilized within the seal bond, preventing longitudinal slippage or delamination during use.

- In a preferred embodiment, the fixed end of each elastic member terminates at a distance of 1 mm to 10 mm inward from the outer side edge of the panel, ensuring that the weld bond fully encapsulates the terminal end without exposing a cut elastic edge, which could otherwise cause skin irritation or fraying.

---

### 4. Welded Bonding Points Between Adjacent Elastic Members (Side Seal Weld Zone)

#### 4.1 Purpose

To enhance the mechanical robustness of the side seal region — which is subjected to repeated tensile loading during wear (e.g., leg movement, waist expansion) — the design incorporates a series of **discrete welded bonding points** intermediate between vertically adjacent elastic members, within the side seal region.

#### 4.2 Structural Description

- The **welded bonding points** (hereinafter "weld points") are formed by ultrasonic or heat-sealing the outer and inner nonwoven layers directly to one another, at locations situated in the width-direction gaps *between* the fixed ends of vertically adjacent elastic members.

- Each weld point is preferably formed as a discrete dot, oval, or bar-shaped fusion bond, having a width-direction dimension smaller than the longitudinal spacing between adjacent elastic members, thereby avoiding direct contact with, or thermal degradation of, the elastic members themselves.

- The weld points are arranged in a **staggered or aligned array** along the height direction of the side seal region, such that:
  - At least one weld point is disposed between each pair of longitudinally adjacent elastic members;
  - The weld points are positioned at a width-direction location coincident with, or laterally outboard of, the fixed ends of the elastic members, such that the weld points reinforce the localized stress concentration region where elastic retraction force is transferred to the nonwoven laminate.

#### 4.3 Functional Effect

This configuration provides the following technical effects:

1. **Delamination Resistance**: By fusing the nonwoven layers directly to each other at points between the elastic strands, the weld points prevent the elastic members from "pulling through" or delaminating the outer and inner nonwoven layers under repeated retraction stress.

2. **Load Distribution**: The discrete weld points distribute the concentrated tensile load at the fixed ends of the elastic members across a broader bonded area of the side seal, reducing the likelihood of localized seal failure (tearing) at the side edge during donning/doffing or dynamic wear.

3. **Maintained Flexibility**: Because the weld points are discrete (rather than a continuous solid bond across the entire side seal height), the side seal region retains a degree of localized flexibility and softness against the wearer's skin, as opposed to a fully rigid, continuously fused panel.

4. **Prevention of Elastic Member Slippage**: The weld points, positioned adjacent to the fixed ends, act as mechanical stoppers that prevent the terminal ends of the elastic members from retracting inward past the side seal boundary over the product's shelf life or during use.

---

### 5. Exemplary Dimensional Parameters (Illustrative, Non-Limiting)

| Parameter | Exemplary Range |
|---|---|
| Elastic member pitch (longitudinal spacing) | 3 mm – 15 mm |
| Elastic member decitex | 300 – 1880 dtex |
| Weld point width-direction dimension | 1 mm – 5 mm |
| Weld point height-direction dimension | 1 mm – 8 mm |
| Distance from panel side edge to fixed end | 1 mm – 10 mm |
| Number of weld points per side seal region | 3 – 20 |

---

### 6. Summary of Inventive Feature

The inventive aspect resides in the **combination** of (i) width-direction elastic members having fixed ends captured within the side seal, and (ii) an array of discrete inter-elastic weld points formed directly between the nonwoven laminate layers in the side seal region, which together achieve a side seal structure exhibiting improved resistance to seal breakage and elastic pull-out, while preserving wearer comfort through retained local flexibility — a balance not achieved through continuous full-panel welding or adhesive-only fixation methods known in the prior art.
